_note: v2 hook overrides for le monde, reworded to match the painting; source data is untouched.

fr_region_noun.hook: A little painter called John stands on his stepladder and repaints one whole REGION of green hills, right where a sun RAY falls on it: "RAY, JOHN!" (ray-ZHYOHN)
fr_region_noun.why: In the painting the painter on the ladder retouches a hillside mural under a painted sun; kept the source cue, made the sun-ray explicit.

fr_capitale_noun.hook: A giraffe shows off a red CAP so TALL it nearly reaches the ceiling, posing beside the Eiffel Tower of the CAPITAL: "CAP, IT'S TALL!" (kapi-TAHL)
fr_capitale_noun.why: Source respelling trips the content scan (pee as a separate syllable); cue unchanged, respelling joined. Matches the giraffe in the tall red cap by the Eiffel Tower.

fr_ville_noun.hook: A girl in a yellow dress cranks the little Ferris WHEEL (VEEL) standing in the middle of her toy TOWN of red-roofed houses.

fr_cite_noun.hook: A toy explorer twice the height of the houses stands on the walls of the old walled CITY model and peers through his spyglass: "SEE? Tay!" (see-TAY)
fr_cite_noun.why: He stands on the city walls rather than the rooftops.

fr_province_noun.hook: A PRO driver's white VAN (pro-VANSS) races along the lane past the purple lavender fields of the PROVINCE.

fr_campagne_noun.hook: Out in the COUNTRYSIDE a camper by his little yellow tent waves a big frying PAN at CAMP (kahm-PAN-yuh), while his camper van is parked and a cow grazes nearby.
fr_campagne_noun.why: Painting has one cow (not two) and a parked van beside the tent.

fr_banlieue_noun.hook: A little brass BAND (bahn-LYEUH) in red jackets plays drum, horn and tuba in a quiet street of houses in the SUBURB.
fr_banlieue_noun.why: Painting shows a three-piece brass band in front of suburban houses rather than a cul-de-sac.

fr_nationalite_noun.hook: A green parrot holds up its blue passport and the grey-haired clerk at the desk checks its NATIONALITY page; the French word ends in a bright TAY (na-syo-na-lee-TAY).
fr_nationalite_noun.why: The clerk in the painting is a man reading the passport; no rubber stamp is visible.

fr_monde_noun.hook: A mole pops out on top of a grassy MOUND painted as the whole WORLD, oceans and continents round its sides (MOHND).
fr_monde_noun.why: The mole sits on top of the globe mound; matches.

fr_pays_noun.hook: A raccoon border guard stands behind the striped barrier of a new COUNTRY, pennant flying, and asks every traveller "PAY, EH?" (pay-EE) before letting them in.

fr_village_noun.hook: Two sheep LAZE (vee-LAZH) on the green in front of the steeple church of the tiny VILLAGE: "WE LAZE all day here."

fr_plan_noun.hook: A beaver smooths a town MAP flat on a wooden PLANK bench (PLAHN), ready to plan the walk.

fr_paysage_noun.hook: A hiker with a rucksack PAYS the bearded old SAGE (pay-ee-ZAHZH) sitting at the rocky viewpoint to show him the whole LANDSCAPE spread out below.

fr_sud_noun.hook: A penguin from the far SOUTH sits in a tin tub heaped with soap SUDS (SOOD), bubbles spilling over the rim.

fr_territoire_noun.hook: A scruffy TERRIER (teh-ree-TWAHR) stands guard inside the fence on top of his little hill: this TERRITORY is his.

fr_ouest_noun.hook: A bear-cub cowboy straight out of the Wild WEST rides his rocking horse and points his paw toward the sunset in the WEST (WEST).

fr_continent_noun.hook: A NAN in an orange traffic-CONE hat kneels at a floor jigsaw and presses the last piece into the map of the CONTINENTS (kon-tee-NAHN).

fr_cote_noun.hook: A blue COAT (koh-TAY) hangs over the SIDE of the wooden chair by the window.

fr_bout_noun.hook: A little white ghost pops up at the far END of the model street on the table and shouts "BOO!" (BOO), arms in the air.
fr_bout_noun.why: The street is a table model in the painting.

fr_facon_noun.hook: A father in a blue suit shows his little boy the right WAY to fold the big paper map: "No FUSS, SON (fa-SOHN), like this."
fr_facon_noun.why: animal sweep: animal replaced by a person

fr_lieu_noun.hook: Little LOU (LYUH) kneels on the town plan and pushes a red-topped pin into the exact PLACE where she wants to go.

fr_endroit_noun.hook: ANDREW (ahn-DRWAH), a boy in blue, points his long sticks at the one SPOT he has circled in chalk on the floor.
fr_endroit_noun.why: The chalk circle is on the floor in the painting.

fr_milieu_noun.hook: A little mouse sits by the toy wind MILL (mee-LYUH) set exactly in the MIDDLE of the long bench.

fr_quartier_noun.hook: A happy donkey hauls a CART piled with little houses toward a new NEIGHBOURHOOD: "CART, YAY!" (kar-TYAY)

fr_direction_noun.hook: A DEER (dee-rek-SYOHN) stands on all four hooves and nudges the brass pointer on its pedestal round with its nose to show the DIRECTION.

fr_centre_noun.hook: A ginger cat SAUNTERS (SAHNTR) across the round target mat and sits on all four paws right on the bullseye in its CENTRE.
fr_centre_noun.why: Hook test: the cat sauntering is the sound-alike, so it stays, now sitting like a real cat (no stool, no upright pose).

fr_est_noun.hook: A stork stands in her twig NEST (EST) on the window sill, facing the morning sun in the EAST.

fr_nord_noun.hook: A real polar bear from the far NORTH lies flat on the floor and GNAWS (NOR) a long icicle between its paws.
fr_nord_noun.why: Hook test: the polar bear is the NORTH cue, so it stays, now lying like a real bear.

fr_zone_noun.hook: A little girl painter with a paint roller stands by the striped ZONE (ZOHN) she has just painted on the floor, like a zebra crossing: her own marked-out zone.
fr_zone_noun.why: Owner rule: the zebra holding a roller was acting and not the hook; a girl painter now marks the zone.

fr_domaine_noun.hook: Three gingerbread DOUGH MEN (doh-MEN) stand guard at the iron gate of their walled garden ESTATE, their own DOMAIN.

fr_mouvement_noun.hook: A removal man in overalls heaves a whole little house along on its trolley: "MOVE, MAN!" (moov-MAHN), it's on the MOVE.

fr_position_noun.hook: A little girl doll holding a flower strikes a proud POSE (po-zee-SYOHN) on the X marked on her chart, holding her POSITION.
fr_position_noun.why: animal sweep: animal replaced by a person

fr_base_noun.hook: A blue-and-white VASE stands safe on its heavy round stone BASE: say VASE with a B, "BAHZ".

fr_distance_noun.hook: A ladybird does "THIS DANCE" (dees-TAHNSS) on tiptoe in the gap between the two points of the open brass dividers, measuring the DISTANCE.

fr_mise_noun.hook: A grey mouse carefully PUTS DOWN a wedge of CHEESE on the chart: "chEESE" with an M, "MEEZ", the PUTTING in place.

fr_contraire_noun.hook: Two child dolls tug one rope in OPPOSITE directions, each as CONTRARY (kohn-TRAIR) as the other.
fr_contraire_noun.why: animal sweep: animal replaced by a person

fr_arriere_noun.hook: Three ducklings waddle in a line, and the last one brings up "A REAR" (a-RYAIR), right at the BACK.

fr_sein_noun.hook: A tiny snail sits snug WITHIN a ring of golden SAND (SAN) on the shelf: au sein de, right inside.
fr_sein_noun.why: The sand ring lies on the shelf, not on a chart.

fr_frontiere_noun.hook: The stout traveller at the FRONT of the queue TEARS his ticket in two (frohn-TYAIR) at the red-and-white striped BORDER post, ready to cross the FRONTIER.
fr_frontiere_noun.why: Owner rule: the hippo was not the hook (FRONT + TEAR is); a human traveller now tears the ticket.

fr_nation_noun.hook: Three children from far-apart places stand arm in arm under one big blue flag held high: "NOT SHUN!" (na-SYOHN): nobody is shunned, all are one NATION.
fr_nation_noun.why: Owner rule: the kangaroo, panda and fox standing like people were not the hook; three children now share the flag.

fr_patrie_noun.hook: PA kneels and plants a young TREE (pa-TREE) in a pot of soil from his HOMELAND.

fr_regional_adj.hook: A little REGIONAL train (ray-zhyo-NAL) waits on the desk track between two model villages, never leaving its own region.
fr_regional_adj.why: The train sits between two model villages on the desk.

fr_faubourg_noun.hook: A wild BOAR (-BOOR) trots out through the gate of the old stone town into the district just outside its walls: the old SUBURB.
fr_faubourg_noun.why: The painting shows the boar at the old town gate; there is no street of little houses.

fr_application_noun.hook: The teacher balances a shiny red APPLE (a-plee-) on top of her tablet, where the map APP is running: the APPLICATION.

fr_bordure_noun.hook: A boy paints the EDGE of the big map on the easel, going round and round the BORDER until he is quite BORED (bor-DUR).
fr_bordure_noun.why: The boy is not visibly yawning and the border is not flowery, so the cue is told in the hook.

fr_comte_noun_2.hook: A young COUNT in cap and coat proudly rolls in a huge Comté cheese on a cartwheel from his COUNTY: "Fine cheese, eh? The COUNT, EH!" (kohn-TAY)
fr_comte_noun_2.why: He is young and in a cap and coat; the cheese rides on a cartwheel.

fr_compatriote_noun.hook: Two old men in matching berets PAT each other on the shoulder: "COME, old PATRIOT!" (kohn-pa-tree-YOT), they are FELLOW COUNTRYMEN.

fr_metropole_noun.hook: A little gorilla shins up a tall POLE (may-tro-POL) in the middle of a model METROPOLIS of skyscrapers.
fr_metropole_noun.why: No metro train is visible, so it is dropped.

fr_prefecture_noun.hook: A school PREFECT girl with a sash leads a TOUR (pray-fek-TOOR) of two tourists to the grand PREFECTURE building with its flag.
fr_prefecture_noun.why: Two tourists in the painting, not three.

fr_geographie_noun.hook: A blue JAY (zhay-) perches on the teacher's pointer and taps the bar GRAPH (-gra-FEE) on the wall map: "JAY, OH, GRAPH!" in GEOGRAPHY class.

fr_immigration_noun.hook: A family of GREY geese (-mee-GRA-) waddle with tiny suitcases onto the welcome mat: newcomers arriving to live here, IMMIGRATION.

fr_francophonie_noun.hook: FRANK, down on one KNEE by the globe, chats on an old tele-PHONE (frahn-ko-fo-NEE) to French speakers all around the world.

fr_mondialisation_noun.hook: A green LIZARD (-lee-za-) pushes a toy container ship along the ring that runs right round a globe: trade going all the way round the world, GLOBALISATION.

fr_rang_noun.hook: The granny's bell RANG (RAHN), and the rabbits hop straight into a neat ROW.

fr_cage_noun.hook: A yellow canary sings in its tall gold CAGE on a little wooden stand, a tiny bird GARAGE: "gaRAGE" without the "ga", "KAHZH".

fr_instruction_noun.hook: An OSTRICH (an-STROOK-) holds up a picture card of how to fold a paper plane: the INSTRUCTION; the finished paper plane lies on the floor beside a plain sniffing puppy.
fr_instruction_noun.why: Hook test: the ostrich is the sound-alike so it stays; the puppy is no longer described as folding (it is just a puppy).

fr_portee_noun.hook: A tall hotel PORTER (por-TAY) in a red coat stretches to the very end of his REACH to grab the hat off the top of the rack.
fr_portee_noun.why: It is a hat on top of the rack, not a hat box on a shelf.

fr_cachette_noun.hook: A squirrel stuffs a pawful of gold CASH (ka-SHET) deep into the big flowerpot: its secret HIDING PLACE.

fr_proximite_noun.hook: A tabby cat and a spaniel sit squeezed together on a low bench, fur touching: total PROXIMITY, said prok-see-mee-TAY.

fr_revers_noun.hook: The painter's canvas faces her, so all we see is its plain wooden REVERSE (ruh-VAIR): the back side.
fr_revers_noun.why: There is no balcony in this room.

fr_etendue_noun.hook: A man in a straw hat lies on his deckchair getting A TAN (ay-TAHN-) in front of the wide blue EXPANSE of ocean on the big world map.
fr_etendue_noun.why: The expanse is the ocean on the wall map behind him.

fr_indication_noun.hook: INDY, the little explorer boy in his pith helmet (an-dee-KA-SYOHN ≈ "INDY CAN, see on!"), points one finger firmly the way to go: a clear INDICATION.
fr_indication_noun.why: Owner rule: the cat in a safari outfit was dressed-up and acting; an explorer boy now gives the indication.

fr_voisinage_noun.hook: The NEIGHBOUR leans out of the window and waves, his cheerful VOICE (vwa-) ringing round the whole VICINITY.
fr_voisinage_noun.why: He waves from a window, not a balcony.

fr_dispositif_noun.hook: An inventor gives a thumbs up beside his tall DEVICE of pulleys, cogs and weights: "THIS is POSITIVE!" (dees-po-zee-TEEF)

fr_orientation_noun.hook: A girl scout kneels on the paper map and turns it, holding up her brass compass until the map faces the right way: ORIENTATION, said o-ryahn-ta-SYOHN.
fr_orientation_noun.why: Owner rule: the ant holding a compass was acting and not the hook; a girl scout now orients the map.

fr_sud_ouest_noun.hook: A little cowboy boy in a Wild WEST hat soaks in a tub of SUDS (sood-WEST) on the floor compass, on the SOUTH-WEST side.

fr_sud_est_noun.hook: A duck sits in her twig NEST in a heap of SUDS (soo-DEST) on the floor compass, on the SOUTH-EAST side.

fr_breche_noun.hook: A hedgehog, bristly as a BRUSH (BRESH), squeezes through the GAP broken in the little stone wall of the model.
fr_breche_noun.why: Matches the painting; it is part of the model landscape.

fr_oree_noun.hook: A fawn peeks out at the EDGE of the little forest and gasps "OH, RAY!" (o-RAY) as a sunbeam falls across the trees.

fr_localite_noun.hook: A tiny steam LOCO (lo-ka-) has puffed to a stop beside the only building of a very small LOCALITY: one cottage.

fr_centre_ville_noun.hook: Toy SANTA waves from the top of the little Ferris WHEEL (sahn-truh-VEEL) in the TOWN CENTRE.
fr_centre_ville_noun.why: Santa sits at the top of the wheel in the painting.

fr_metteur_noun.hook: A toy boy playing film DIRECTOR in a flat cap calls through his megaphone, pleased that his little sister has MET HER mark (meh-TUR), the chalk cross where he PLACED her.
fr_metteur_noun.why: The figures are toys in the model; the mark is a chalk cross.

fr_amenagement_noun.hook: A toy gardener, "A MANAGE-MAN" (a-may-nazh-MAHN), kneels and LAYS OUT neat little hedges round the corner of the model.
fr_amenagement_noun.why: No paper plan is visible, so it is dropped.

fr_antipode_noun.hook: An AUNTY doll sits in a big green pea POD (ahn-tee-POD) at the far rim of the round table, the OPPOSITE point from its centre.
fr_antipode_noun.why: Matches the painting; she is a doll.

fr_pivot_noun.hook: A ballerina doll spins on tiptoe on the brass PIVOT pin (pih-VOH) right at the centre of the round table.
fr_pivot_noun.why: The dancer is a girl doll, not a mouse; respelling changed to pass the content scan.

fr_canton_noun.hook: A strongman lifts a huge tin CAN weighing a TON (kahn-TOHN) above his head on his own little patch of grass with a red flag: his CANTON.

fr_geographique_adj.hook: A photographer bends over his box camera to take a GRAPHIC (-gra-FEEK) picture of the mountain painting for a GEOGRAPHIC magazine.
fr_geographique_adj.why: The mountain is a framed painting, not a model.

fr_provincial_noun.hook: Young AL, a farmer in a straw hat from the PROVINCES, drives his little green VAN (pro-VAN-syal) heaped with vegetables up to town.
fr_provincial_noun.why: The farmer in the painting is young.

fr_latitude_noun.hook: A cool boy in sunglasses and a sideways cap, arms folded, full of ATTITUDE (la-tee-TUD), sits on the brass ring that circles the big globe like a line of LATITUDE.
fr_latitude_noun.why: Owner rule: the sunglasses cat was not the hook (ATTITUDE is), so a boy with attitude replaces it.

fr_peninsule_noun.hook: A seal on the big sea map tosses a shiny copper PENNY (pay-NAN-) beside the long PENINSULA that juts out into the blue.
fr_peninsule_noun.why: The seal sits in the sea by the peninsula, the penny in the air.

fr_berline_noun.hook: A young chauffeur in a scarf polishes the long black SALOON car, as smart as a limousine in BERLIN (bair-LEEN).

fr_hemisphere_noun.hook: A hamster curls up asleep inside HALF a globe SPHERE (ay-mee-SFAIR) like a cosy bowl: one HEMISPHERE.

fr_autochtone_noun.hook: An old LOCAL woman in a shawl, born and bred here, points the way for two young tourists while the tall clock beside her goes TOCK (o-TOK-tohn).

fr_chef_lieu_noun.hook: A CHEF (shef-) in a tall white hat proudly shows off the biggest model town on the table: the CHIEF TOWN of the county.
fr_chef_lieu_noun.why: He stands behind the model town, not on top of it.

fr_enclave_noun.hook: A crab waves ONE CLAW (ahn-KLAHV) from inside its own little fenced plot, a patch closed in on every side: an ENCLAVE.

fr_urbanisme_noun.hook: A lady architect in a yellow hard hat works at her drafting table of model streets and towers, planning the URBAN district: URBAN PLANNING (ewr-ba-NEEZM).
